title: Adapting the length of antibiotics for respiratory tract infections in primary care.
official: Tailoring antibiotic duration for respiratory tract infections in primary care. A pragmatic randomised clinical trial [STORM Study]
summary: Main objective: To assess the overall assessment of the clinical efficacy at day 14
conditions: Acute lower Respiratory Tract Infection or acute rhinosinusitis
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ranging from 18 to 75 years of age
2. Acute lower Respiratory Tract Infection or acute bacterial rhinosinusitis
3. GPs deem a beta-lactam therapy for at least seven days is necessary
Exclusion criteria:
1. Respiratory Tract Infections different from a lower RTI or acute rhinosinusitis
2. Inability/unable to understand and/or take part in the clinical trial
3. Currently participating in another clinical trial
4. Previously participated in the STORM study
5. Active neoplasia
6. Terminal illness
7. Institutionalized patient
8. Inability to understand and/or participate in the clinical trial
9. The doctor decides not to give an antibiotic for this RTI
10. Patients with suspected septicaemia, based on the Quick SOFA scale; patients with two or more of the following criteria must be excluded: a) respiratory rate ≥22 breaths/minute; b) systolic blood pressure <100 mm Hg, and/or c) altered mental status with a Glasgow score <15)
11. Patients with a severe community-acquired pneumonia, based on the CRB65 scale: patients with any of the following criterion must be excluded: a) confusion; b) respiratory rate ≥30 breaths/minute; c) systolic blood pressure <90 mm Hg or diastolic ≤60 mm Hg; and/or d) age ≥65 years
12. Patients with COPD who have taken four or more antibiotic courses in the previous year, presence of significant bronchiectasis, and/or isolation of Pseudomonas in a previous sputum culture
13. Patients with reported allergy to beta-lactams
14. Patients who have taken an antibiotic in the previous two weeks
15. A working diagnosis of a non-infective disorder, such as heart failure, pulmonary embolus, oesophageal reflux
16. Immunocompromised patients, such as HIV infection, patients taking immunosuppressive treatment, antineoplastic therapy, or systemic corticosteroids
